subject: history
title: Industrial Breakthroughs Adventure
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet Jenner, Snow, Pasteur and Lister — the breakthrough generation.
meta_desc: GCSE History — vaccination, germ theory and antiseptic surgery.
final_note: You learned how vaccination, germ theory and antiseptics transformed medicine.

Identified TB bacterium in 1882, cholera in 1883
1867 used carbolic acid as an antiseptic in surgery

walkthroughs.body_html:
In 1796 Edward Jenner noticed milkmaids who had cowpox did not get smallpox.

He tested it on James Phipps and published in 1798. In 1853 smallpox vaccination became compulsory for babies in Britain.

In 1854 John Snow mapped cholera deaths around the Broad Street pump in Soho.

In 1861 Pasteur published Germ Theory. Robert Koch then identified the bacteria for anthrax (1876), TB (1882) and cholera (1883).

In 1867 Joseph Lister sprayed carbolic acid in operating theatres — infection deaths plunged.

Anaesthetics (chloroform, 1847) and antiseptics enabled deeper surgery. Parliament passed the 1875 Public Health Act, forcing councils to provide clean water and sewers.

Tuberculosis
Anthrax

mcqs.q: Why was Jenner's smallpox vaccination significant in 1796?
options: Cities were unhealthy because factory smoke poisoned the food.
Jenner discovered germs and used them to make vaccines.
He showed cowpox material could prevent smallpox safely — the first effective vaccine, though he did not know why it worked; germ theory came nearly a century later.
Jenner used penicillin to cure smallpox.

mcqs.q: Why did public health reforms accelerate after 1848?
options: The 1875 Act made the NHS free for all workers.
The 1848 Public Health Act followed cholera epidemics and Chadwick's report; John Snow's 1854 Broad Street pump study reinforced the case for clean water by 1875.
Cities were unhealthy because factory smoke poisoned the food.
Public health acts were passed because Victorians discovered germs in the 1840s.

mcqs.q: Why were 19th-century industrial cities so unhealthy?
options: Rapid population growth outpaced housing, water and sewage; lack of regulation produced overcrowded slums and cholera epidemics until reforms followed Chadwick's 1842 report.
Cities were unhealthy because factory smoke poisoned the food.
Cities were unhealthy because Victorians did not care about hygiene.
The 1875 Act made the NHS free for all workers.
